data.name: MNIST Database of Handwritten Digits
data.abstract: Well-known database of 70,000 handwritten digits (10 class labels) with each example represented as an image of 28 x 28 gray-scale pixels.

intro_paper.title: Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition
intro_paper.authors: Y. LeCun, L. Bottou, Y. Bengio, P. Haffner

additional_info.purpose: As a testbed for development of handwriting recognition algorithms and machine learning classification algorithms in general.
additional_info.funded_by: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) originally, and later, AT&T Bell Labs
additional_info.instances_represent: 28 x 28 gray-scale centered images of handwritten digites
additional_info.recommended_data_splits: Yes. A specific split with 60,000 for training, 10,000 for testing.
additional_info.preprocessing_description: The original NIST data was preprocessed by Yann LeCun and colleagues at AT&T Bell Labs: see http://yann.lecun.com/exdb/mnist/ for details
